subject: Lighthouse: urgent cross-region failover & exec bridge request
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@lighthouse.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@lighthouse.ai
Date: 2028-03-19T08:15:00Z
Subject: Major latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (customer impact)

Avery,

We’re seeing a sustained latency increase (p90 ~1.8s -> 5.6s) across our production customers since 07:40 PT and a rise in 5xx to ~7%. Error-rate correlates with requests routed to us-west-2. This is impacting checkout flows for several merchants. Our engineering team is monitoring on our side — we need Redwood to confirm: is this an internal regional issue or a model/serving degradation?

We need an actionable mitigation within the next 60 minutes and executive visibility: our CEO is on the line for an update. Please escalate.

Attached: short CSV with request counts and error rates (lighthouse_kpi_snapshot.csv).

—Elena Morris
Head of Product Ops, Lighthouse AI
Elena Morris | Lighthouse AI
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@lighthouse.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-19T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Major latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (customer impact)

Thanks Elena — apologies for the disruption. We’re escalating to ops and eng immediately.

Action so far:
- Hannah/ops: kicked off regional triage and verified elevated 5xx and tail latencies in us-west-2.
- Vivek/eng: looking at model-serving nodes and KV cache saturation.
- I’m standing up a brief exec bridge + customer bridge now (15 min). Will send dial-in and plan.

Proposed immediate mitigation: short traffic diversion from us-west-2 to us-east-1 for your traffic to lower customer impact while we fix root cause. Need customer go-ahead to authorize cross-region shift. Estimated switch: 8–12 minutes to ramp (will use graceful drain).

If we don’t hear back in 8 minutes, we’ll proceed with a controlled partial diversion to preserve your checkout flow.

—Avery Johnson

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-19T08:27:00Z
Subject: RE: Major latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (customer impact)

Avery / team — quick triage:
- Region: us-west-2, AZ b & c show the highest error/concurrency.
- Symptoms: KV cache miss rate up x11, instance queuing rising, L7 retries increased.
- Models: Multiple model variants show increased jitter; not limited to a single model binary.
- Early hypothesis: overloaded pool due to sudden traffic fanout + cache eviction storm.

Mitigations in flight:
1) Increase instance concurrency cap on the hot pool (5 min).
2) Expand pool with reserved nodes (10–15 min).
3) Prepare cross-region traffic diversion plan (needs exec ok).

Requesting: exec-level approval to start staged cross-region diversion to us-east-1 for Lighthouse traffic only (start 10% -> 50% over 6 minutes). I’ll provide a timeline and rollback criterion.

Attachment: us-west-2_failover_trace.log (tail of server logs).

—Hannah
Senior Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-19T08:34:00Z
Subject: RE: Major latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (customer impact)

On Mar 19, 2028, Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> Avery / team — quick triage:
> - Region: us-west-2, AZ b & c show the highest error/concurrency.
> - Symptoms: KV cache miss rate up x11, instance queuing rising, L7 retries increased.

We’re seeing K/V eviction churn from a hot prefix set combined with an unlucky slot allocation that increased memory pressure on several GPU hosts. This has pushed inference tasks into slower fallback kernels, increasing p95/p99 and causing some 5xx when queue deadlines are hit.

Short-term action (I can execute with ops):
- Start staged cross-region diversion for Lighthouse (us-west-2 -> us-east-1): 10% immediate, monitor 3 min, then step to 30%, then 60% if metrics good.
- Apply temporary cache pinning for top prefixes (will reduce evictions).
- Ramp additional quantized worker pool in us-east-1 to absorb diverted traffic.

Risks: slight model variant mismatch for a small subset of requests — we’ll apply a content-safe validation during the ramp and auto-fallback on quality regressions.

I’ll prepare the traffic plan PDF (proposed_traffic_plan.pdf) and can be on the bridge. Requesting signoff to proceed.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

To: Elena Morris <elena@lighthouse.ai>, Tom Hughes <tom.hughes@lighthouse.ai>, support@lighthouse.ai

Date: 2028-03-19T08:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Major latency + 5xx spike — US-WEST-2 (customer impact)

Elena / Tom — we propose the following immediate mitigation (requires your permission):
- Stage 1 (T+0): Divert 10% of Lighthouse traffic from us-west-2 to us-east-1 (8–12 min ramp window).
- Stage 2 (T+3m): If p95 and 5xx improve, step to 30% and apply cache pinning.
- Stage 3 (T+10m): If stable, step to 60% and continue monitoring; full drain possible if needed.

Monitoring & rollback: Real-time dashboards and quality checks. Auto-rollback on >0.5% quality regression or customer error uptick.

Please reply with: APPROVE/DENY. If we don’t get a reply in 8 minutes we’ll proceed with a conservative 10% diversion to protect checkout flows.

Dial-in (Ops bridge): +1 650-555-0100 (Bridge ID 982-330)

Attachment: proposed_traffic_plan.pdf

Date: 2028-03-19T12:03:00Z
Subject: Post-action exec note — Lighthouse us-west-2 incident

Summary for execs & commercial: (brief)
- Incident: KV-cache eviction storm in us-west-2 increased p95/p99 and 5xx for Lighthouse traffic.
- Immediate action: Controlled cross-region diversion (us-west-2 -> us-east-1) started at 08:50 PT; stepped 10% -> 30% -> 60%; checkout p95 returned to ~1.6s within 9 minutes of first diversion and 5xx dropped to baseline.
- Root cause: resource allocation edge-case + hot-prefix churn; mitigations: cache pinning, pool sizing fix, allocator patch being rolled.
- Customer impact: transient; Lighthouse confirmed restored checkout; they will review for any downstream evidence of content drift.
- Commercial: recommend goodwill credit for the 2-hr impact window and a follow-up technical review with Lighthouse next week (Mar 26).

Attachments: incident timeline & timeline CSV included.

Recommended next steps (ops + eng + AM):
1) Engineering to ship allocator patch today (Vivek) and schedule a hotfix rollout in staging+canary.
2) Ops to run a forced traffic-sim for Lighthouse-like pattern to validate.
3) AM (Marissa) to coordinate customer credit & exec summary for their leadership.

—Markus Klein
VP, Site Reliability & Security, Redwood Inference
